stories.delivered_paragraph: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said the company has never sought a blanket ban on open-weight AI models, responding to criticism after Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta and others urged Washington against early restrictions. Amodei said models without dangerous capabilities can be a public good, while arguing policymakers should focus on specific high-risk capabilities rather than whether a model is open or closed. The dispute reflects growing pressure on U.S. officials as Chinese open-weight models become more competitive.

stories.delivered_paragraph: X has begun rolling out X Money to U.S. Premium and Premium Plus subscribers, expanding Elon Musk’s effort to turn the social platform into an all-purpose app. The service offers a digital wallet, free person-to-person transfers, Apple Wallet support and a metal Visa card; it advertises yields of up to 6% APY for eligible users. The launch moves X into a tightly regulated payments market and is likely to renew scrutiny over consumer safeguards.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon has cut Razer’s wired Huntsman V3 Pro TKL gaming keyboard to $124.99 from $159.99, a discount of more than 20%. Its optical analog switches let users set key activation points from 0.1mm to 4mm and reset keys before they return fully upward, features aimed at faster competitive play. The deal makes a specialized adjustable-switch keyboard cheaper, though it remains a compact, wired model designed for gamers rather than general office use.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Seattle police now believe at least three people fired shots during Sunday’s shooting at the Bite of Seattle festival near the Space Needle, revising their earlier assessment of two suspects exchanging fire. Three people were killed and at least four wounded, including a two-year-old; one 15-year-old suspect is in custody, one suspected shooter was killed, and police are seeking at least one more person. The expanded investigation leaves a major public-event shooting case unresolved.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A Los Angeles judge ruled that singer D4vd, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, must stand trial on murder charges in the death of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Prosecutors allege Burke killed and dismembered her after years of sexual abuse; her remains were found last September in a Tesla registered to his address. Burke, 21, has pleaded not guilty, with arraignment set for August 31 and trial due within 90 days afterward.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Several small businesses have filed new lawsuits challenging the Trump administration’s latest import tariffs, which impose rates of 10% or 12.5% on goods from more than 60 economies. The plaintiffs include spice seller Burlap & Barrel, watch retailer Collective Horology and toymaker Learning Resources, which previously won a Supreme Court challenge to tariffs imposed under a different law. Their cases test whether the administration can sustain its trade policy under Section 301 authority.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A federal magistrate judge has ordered Donald Trump’s trust to give the BBC some business financial records for the network’s defense against his $10 billion defamation lawsuit, while narrowing the scope of the BBC’s subpoena. The ruling grants the broadcaster part of its request for documents that could bear on claimed damages. It advances discovery without deciding whether the BBC defamed Trump or whether he can establish the financial harm alleged.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Senior U.S. officials believe economic pressure may inflict more lasting damage on Iran’s government than the recent bombing campaign, as reports point to worsening shortages, including gasoline, inside the oil-rich country. President Trump paused U.S. strikes after 13 consecutive days and said Tehran had sought talks, a claim Iran denied. Oman, Qatar and Pakistan are mediating efforts to turn the pause into a durable ceasefire, with Strait of Hormuz shipping among the issues under discussion.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Shots were fired at the U.S. consulate in Toronto for the second time this year, and police say the suspected attacker escaped after a high-speed chase. Three people were arrested after a similar June attack, making the repeat targeting a security concern for U.S. diplomatic facilities and a continuing investigation for Toronto police.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The accelerating AI race is reshaping U.S.-China competition beyond the long-running dispute over tariffs, with both countries treating advanced computing and AI models as national strategic priorities. The debate increasingly centers on who controls the technology, chips and infrastructure needed to develop frontier systems rather than simply the trade flows between the two economies. That shift could make technology policy a more important source of friction in the bilateral relationship.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Major League Baseball’s trade market remains relatively quiet with the Aug. 3 deadline a week away, largely because all but eight teams were within four games of a playoff spot entering Monday. That parity has left clubs waiting for the next few games to decide whether to buy or sell, even as stars such as Detroit pitcher Tarik Skubal draw speculation. The compressed standings could delay major deals until contenders have clearer postseason odds.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Ariana Grande has sued unidentified hackers in Los Angeles, alleging they repeatedly stole and leaked unreleased songs, photographs and video by targeting her producers and photographers. Her complaint says 45 songs were leaked in 2023 alone and seeks to identify the anonymous defendants through subpoenas to internet service providers. The case is aimed first at unmasking the alleged hackers, potentially setting up later claims for damages and deterrence against music leaks.

stories.delivered_paragraph: National League contenders including the Braves, Phillies, Dodgers, Brewers and Cubs are weighing how aggressively to act before MLB’s Aug. 3 trade deadline. With much of the league still close to a playoff place, front offices have limited clarity on whether to spend heavily for immediate upgrades or preserve prospects. The Brewers’ willingness to make a major move and the Braves’ appetite to go all-in are among the decisions likely to shape the pennant race.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Marvel Studios has outlined parts of its post-Avengers: Secret Wars slate, confirming Black Panther 3 for Dec. 15, 2028 and a Ryan Gosling-led Ghost Rider film for sometime that year. stories.delivered_paragraph: SK Hynix shares fell 10% in Seoul on Tuesday as a wider semiconductor selloff extended after another weak Wall Street session. The decline hit a major supplier of advanced memory chips, a crucial part of the hardware chain supporting AI data centers, while other South Korean chip shares also dropped. The move shows how quickly investor concern can spread through a sector whose valuations have been lifted by expectations for sustained AI demand.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Investors are focused on reports that Nvidia could backstop an OpenAI data-center lease, an arrangement that would reportedly be the largest of its kind and has prompted a bubble warning from one analyst. The concern is that a chipmaker supporting financing for customers’ infrastructure could echo practices associated with past technology booms. Any deal remains prospective, but it would intensify scrutiny of whether AI spending is being supported by circular or unusually risky financing.
